subject: Request: custom SLA annex & order form language for Planar Health
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@planarhealth.com>
To: naomi.feldman@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: custom SLA annex & order form language for Planar Health

Hi Naomi / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Planar Health is excited about Redwood for clinical NLP inference. Procurement asked me to send the SLA conditions they need before we can route this to legal. High-level asks: 

- Monthly uptime: 99.95% (measured at the public endpoint).
- Latency: p95 text-gen < 350ms for requests up to 512 tokens; p99 target included in premium tier.
- Evidence: quarterly uptime reports, access to infra-level outage logs on request, and SOC 2 Type II report.
- Order form needs explicit line items for dedicated capacity (we expect sustained 100 req/s peak), and a definition of latency SLOs per route/model.

Can you provide a redlined SLA annex, and the exact order form language we should put in our PO? Procurement also wants to know what remediation/credits look like for partial downtime vs full outage.

Attaching our preliminary PO (Purchase_Order_5678.pdf) for reference.

If we can get a draft annex + order form text by EOD tomorrow, procurement will start legal review.

Best,
Elena Ruiz
Head of Platform Integrations
Planar Health

Attachments: Purchase_Order_5678.pdf (pdf)
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@planarhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-20T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: custom SLA annex & order form language for Planar Health

Elena — thanks for the clear ask and the PO. We're happy to get you a draft annex and order form language. Quick clarifying Qs before we produce the redline:

1) When you say 100 req/s peak, is that sustained over minutes (100 RPS sustained for 10m) or bursts to 100 RPS? Do you expect warm KV caches or cold-start behavior?
2) Which models/routes are critical to include in the SLO (e.g., api/v1/generate-text vs embeddings)?

Our plan: we will send a redlined SLA annex that includes: uptime measurement method, latency tiers, credit calculations for partial and full outages, and an evidence-playbook section that specifies what logs and reports are provided and timelines. Karthik will scope technical constraints that need to be reflected in the order form (reserved capacity, minimum commitments).

I've attached our starting draft: Planar_SLA_Annex_Draft_v1.docx. Ben — looping you for procurement language and pricing line items.

Naomi Feldman
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0124

Attachments: Planar_SLA_Annex_Draft_v1.docx (docx)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-21T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: custom SLA annex & order form language for Planar Health

Naomi / Ben — technical notes for the redline (putting these here so legal/procurement have exact language options):

- Latency SLOs need to be conditional on model family, max tokens, and whether requests are served from Dedicated vs Hosted. Suggested clause: "Latency SLO (p95) applies to requests served from Dedicated capacity with pre-warmed KV caches and max prompt+completion length <= 512 tokens."
- For hosted/shared capacity we recommend a lower SLO (e.g., p95 < 450ms) and an explicit fallback policy when competing workloads cause degradation.
- Credit calculations: propose a tiered credit table (partial-credit bands for 99.9-99.95, higher credits below 99.9). Credits should cap at monthly invoice amount; for Dedicated, include additional remediation options (priority scheduling, capacity uplift credits).
- Order form line items to be explicit: "Dedicated GPU pool: X vGPU-equivalent units; Target throughput: Y req/s; Model families supported: [gpt-family, redwood-llama-variants]". Also call out expected warm-up window and KV cache warming (e.g., 30 minutes for cold starts).

I'm attaching a short notes file with suggested wording (technical-sla-notes.txt). Legal will need to convert these into indemnities/limitations where appropriate.

—Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments: technical-sla-notes.txt (txt)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@planarhealth.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@planarhealth.com>
Date: 2027-04-21T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: custom SLA annex & order form language for Planar Health

Elena — thanks for the PO and the timing. We've incorporated Karthik's notes into a redline and an order form snippet. High-level items included in the attached OrderForm_v3.pdf:

- Dedicated pool: 2x reserved A10G-equivalent vGPUs (configurable at execution)
- Throughput guarantee: 100 req/s sustained, 200 req/s burst allowance for 5 minutes
- Latency SLO: p95 < 350ms for Dedicated (<=512 tokens); p95 < 450ms for Hosted fallback
- Credit table: tiered credits and cap at monthly invoice; for Dedicated customers there is an option to request priority remediation scheduling (non-financial remedial action)

Next steps we recommend:
- Procurement confirms the exact throughput profile (sustained vs burst) and preferred credit cap.
- We prepare a DocuSign-ready annex and an order form PDF for signature.

Link to the DocuSign draft will be shared when you confirm throughput.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Attachments: OrderForm_v3.pdf (pdf)
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@planarhealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@planarhealth.com>, Greg Thompson <greg.thompson@planarhealth.com>
Date: 2027-04-22T08:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: custom SLA annex & order form language for Planar Health

Thanks Ben / Naomi — the draft looks close. A few follow-ups from procurement/legal: 

1) We need explicit language on the cadence and format of evidence requests (e.g., within 10 business days Redwood will provide stack traces and outage logs for the affected period).
2) Credits: procurement prefers a formula that ties credits to minutes of degraded service rather than a flat monthly cap; are you open to a minutes-based partial credit for incidents below a threshold?
3) Please include an exhibit that defines measurement points (which endpoints and probe methodology).

Procurement copied here will confirm sustained vs burst. For now, we can say sustained 100 req/s over a 10-minute window with bursts to 200 for up to 5 minutes.

If we can get a revised annex addressing 1–3 and a DocuSign link by Thursday EOD (our legal needs 48 hours), we can move to signature next week.

Best regards,
Elena Ruiz
Head of Platform Integrations
Planar Health

Attachments: Purchase_Order_5678.pdf (pdf)
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@planarhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@planarhealth.com>
Date: 2027-04-22T17:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: custom SLA annex & order form language for Planar Health

Elena — appreciate the quick clarifications. We can accommodate the minutes-based partial-credit formula and will add a concise evidence-playbook exhibit that specifies timelines (10 business days for logs, SOC2 delivery timelines, sample reports).

To summarize next steps and timeline: 
- Today (EOD): we will update the annex to include measurement-point exhibit, minutes-based credit formula, and evidence-playbook.
- Tomorrow: Legal will review final redline; Ben will generate DocuSign order form (OrderForm_v3 -> OrderForm_final).
- Thursday EOD: target DocuSign link provided to Planar for signature.

Please confirm procurement contact name and email so we can pre-populate the DocuSign. Once signed we will schedule a technical onboarding call to review KV cache warm-up behavior and production ramp.

Thanks — Naomi
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com
